column1: # Game profile of Metroid Dread (Switch, base game v0 + update 2.1.0 = v327680). Bring-up has just started: the memory values are Mario's until measured
# MercurySteam's own engine, SDK 11.4.3, NVN; scripts are Lua 5.1 bytecode (.lc), audio is NintendoWare Atk. Every shader is in system/shd/*.bshdat (MSHD containers, read by shader_split.py)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 2.1.0 copy is extracted; the base game's own build IDs are added when needed
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie 11.4.3)

# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0), so there is no virtual address memory: the game uses SetHeapSize. main's bss is about 1.8 GB (0x70cd2fa0, the engine's static heap); it is part of the module image, not of the block below.

# Measured (DM_SVC=1): the alias region gets one page (4 KB) mapped during SDK initialization; thread stacks go into the stack region through MapMemory; the heap request is pool − used = 0x58800000 (1.38 GB, with the 1.8 GB bss counted as used).

# So the block needs only 2.25 GB = 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 1.5 GB heap region; with main's 1.9 GB image that is about 4.3 GB, below the 5 GB proven on a phone (D2R). The application pool is still the Switch's 3285 MB
